mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 1.5%) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20d forward returns is >= -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tight labor market that boosts corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase fails to produce positive 20d returns in more than 50% of instances (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: High consumer spending (RSAFS above 500,000 million dollars) during late-cycle expansions correlates with rising corporate revenues, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars and GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% annually), the 20d forward returns are not significantly positive (mean return <=0, p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (INDPRO < 100) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, correlating with higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between HOUST and 20d forward returns is not significantly positive (Rank IC <= 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 1.5%) and declining unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals monetary tightening during a strong labor market, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and UNRATE < 4.0% fails to produce negative 20d returns in more than 50% of instances (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: High consumer spending (RSAFS above 500,000 million dollars) during early-cycle expansions correlates with accelerating corporate revenues, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansions (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars and GDP growth rate > 1.0% annually), the 20d forward returns are not significantly positive (mean return <=0, p>0.05).
